comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Configurability was asked for alongside this and is filed separately as `a_2Ibt8w4oi`.

They are separate on purpose. Letting somebody pick their own colours does not fix this one: the focus ring follows the macOS accent, which Muster does not choose, so any fixed state palette collides with some accent - green with `done`, orange with `blocked`. This card is about the two rings differing in kind rather than only in hue.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A focused pane and a working pane are both edged in blue, so a focused working agent is four points of blue and neither ring means anything. Reported as *"the focus border is blue but that's also the border color of an agent working, which looks a little confusing"*.

    PaneChrome.swift:31    working    -> NSColor.systemBlue
    PaneChrome.swift:249   focused    -> NSColor.controlAccentColor   (blue by default)

The two rings are adjacent, inset by `borderWidth` (2pt), so they read as one thick edge.

The design already anticipated this and the comment on `PaneChrome` says so:

> Two edges, not one, and they mean different things. The outer is the agent's state, which is the whole point of the product; the inner says which pane a keystroke would go to. One edge carrying both would make a working pane and a focused pane indistinguishable, which is exactly the confusion these are for clearing up.

Splitting them into two rings was right. Painting both blue puts the confusion back.

## Why hue alone will not fix it

`controlAccentColor` is the macOS accent, which the person using Muster chooses in System Settings. Muster does not pick it and cannot know it. So:

- On the default accent it collides with `working`.
- Set the accent to green and it collides with `done` instead.
- Set it to orange and it collides with `blocked`.

Any fixed state palette collides with *some* accent. Moving `working` off blue fixes the common case and leaves the same bug for anybody whose accent happens to match another state - and they will report it as a different bug.

So the rings should differ in **kind**, not only colour: thickness, an inset gap, a dash, or drawing focus on one edge rather than four. Then the accent can be anything and focus still reads as focus. What that should look like is a design call rather than something to settle in a ticket.

## Changing the default is still worth doing

Whatever the rings end up looking like, `working` being blue has a second, independent reason to move. From `a_2HPHq3Zck`, which set the legend:

> plain ANSI blue (34) is the least legible of the sixteen on a dark background, and `working` is the state a window spends most of its time in

Two arguments for the same change, arrived at separately.

What it costs, because the legend is deliberately duplicated and pinned: `PaneChrome.swift:29`, `crates/muster-cli/src/render.rs` (`agent_style`), `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/cli/window.md`, and a tripwire test on each side that fails if its own row moves. `a_2HPHq3Zck` established that arrangement on purpose - nothing can check the two across the language line - so a colour change is a five-file change by design, not by accident.

## Validating a fix

- A focused working pane is distinguishable from an unfocused working pane at a glance, and from a focused idle one.
- The same holds with the macOS accent set to green and to orange, not only the default.
- Both surfaces still agree on the legend, and both tripwire tests still pass with their rows updated together.
- `muster window` in a dark terminal still reads `working` legibly, which is the other half of the reason to move it.
title: 🟦 A focused pane and a working pane are the same blue, so neither ring reads
